chart.reason: The dataset is dense, ranked, time-indexed quantitative cinema data — the spine of the story is comparative numbers across 89 years.

image.reason: Cinema is inherently visual — atmospheric stills frame the analytical core without competing with the data.

video.reason: No process or transformation is at the centre of the story; static images give the right mood at lower cost and avoid copyright entanglements with real film footage.

audio.reason: The story is about cultural memory measured through references; sound would be decorative, not explanatory. Refraining from the click-to-play audio card pattern.

interactive_or_map.reason: The year-by-year winners table benefits from a sortable/filterable interactive; the hook benefits from a guess-first quiz that sets the surprise.

media_blockers.reason: First teaser prompt was rejected by Gemini content filter (PROHIBITED_CONTENT — blocked likely on Oscar trademark/Best-Picture statuette imagery).
media_blockers.attempted_command: generate_image.py --prompt 'A dimly lit, vintage movie theater scene. A single, weathered Best Picture Oscar statuette...'
media_blockers.fallback_des: des_02 (used a softer abstract theater image without explicit Oscar branding)

des_01.label: Teaser hero — empty theater, single light

content.prompt: A dimly lit, vintage red-velvet movie theater interior. Empty rows of plush red seats face an old projection screen showing a soft amber glow. A single golden trophy figurine, abstract and stylized, sits alone on the front edge of the stage, illuminated by one warm spotlight.

des_01.brief: Cinematic still of an empty theater with a small golden figurine on the stage edge. Full-bleed, no text overlay. Mood: ceremonial space without an audience — the Academy honoring films the world is no longer in the room for.
des_01.rationale: A still image creates the mood (canon-making, but in a half-empty room) without forcing motion or running into trademark issues with explicit Oscar imagery.

des_02.label: Hook chart — biggest snubs ratio bar chart

highlight.row: 1980 Empire Strikes Back vs Ordinary People

content.interaction: hover tooltip showing exact counts and shares for both films

style.palette: amber + cool grey on dark background

des_02.brief: Horizontal dumbbell or paired-bar chart. Each row is a year. Two bars per row: the year's most-referenced film (amber) and the actual Best Picture winner (grey). Years sorted by the count_ratio (biggest gap on top). Annotate the 1980 row prominently. Show 15 rows. Reader can hover any row to see exact reference counts.
des_02.rationale: A dumbbell chart makes the gap visceral — readers see how far the winner falls below the year-#1. This is the core indictment of the piece.

des_03.label: Stat callout — 58.4% of years

content.label: of years from 1928 to 2016, the most-referenced film was not even nominated for Best Picture

des_03.brief: Large 80px stat: 58.4% in amber, smaller editorial caption underneath. Sits between the hook prose and the chart.
des_03.rationale: The number is the headline — better as a typographic moment than as another chart.

des_04.label: Methodology card — what counts as a reference

content.initial_state: Two side-by-side cards: a Casablanca quote and a Frasier quote with arrow between them
content.trigger: hover or tap reveals the underlying connection (one IMDb 'connection' = one count)
content.transition: subtle annotation lines link the two quotes
content.payoff: readers grok the proxy: every connection in the data is a moment like this

des_04.brief: Editorial annotation with two quote cards. Left card: 'Of all the gin joints in all the towns in all the world, she walks into mine.' — Casablanca (1942). Right card: 'Of all the coffee joints in all the towns in all the world…' — Niles, Frasier (1990s). An arrow + label says: 'one IMDb connection.' Below: 'Casablanca: 1,454 connections like this.' Light interactive: hover/tap lights up the parallel words.
des_04.rationale: This is methodology — the reader needs to feel that 'reference' is a real, observable thing, not an abstract stat.

des_05.label: Decade hit-rate chart

content.color: two metrics (mean rank: navy line; pct rank-1: amber bars)
content.interaction: hover bar/point shows exact decade values

style.palette: navy + amber on warm cream background

des_05.brief: Combined chart with decade on x-axis. Amber bars: pct of winners that were the year-#1 film. Navy line + dots: mean year_rank of winners. Two y-axes. Annotate the 1980s and 2010s columns: 'zero rank-#1 winners.' The story arc — sharp 1970s, collapse 1980s, partial recovery, collapse again 2010s — is read off this chart.
des_05.rationale: The hit-rate decline is the analytical spine. A combo chart compresses two metrics that tell the same story without needing two chart blocks.

des_06.label: Year-by-year share line chart with named winners

content.interaction: hover any dot for film name, year, share, year_rank

des_06.brief: Time series. X-axis: oscars_year 1928-2016. Y-axis: annual_share of the Best Picture winner (0-50%). Each winner is a dot, sized by share. Color encodes year_rank bin (amber = #1, faded toward grey for #11+). A LOWESS trend line drops smoothly. Casablanca peak labeled at 48.7%. Cavalcade labeled at the bottom (0.3%, year 1933). Spotlight and Moonlight labeled at the right. Reader can hover any dot.
des_06.rationale: This is the most data-rich chart in the piece — it shows trajectory, magnitude, and outliers in one frame, with the named winners that anchor the prose.

des_07.label: Image divider — two reels

content.prompt: Abstract editorial illustration: two parallel film reels unspooling on a deep navy background. The top reel is golden and bright with cinematic frames; the lower reel is pale grey, muted, sparse.

des_07.brief: Full-width image break between the year-by-year chart and the next analytical section. Decorative, sets up the parallel-canon idea (the films audiences remember vs. the films the Academy chose).
des_07.rationale: After two consecutive charts, the page needs a visual pause; this image does double duty as an editorial metaphor for the two parallel canons.

des_08.label: Outside-top-10 winners — ranked bar chart

content.interaction: hover for full count and annual_share

des_08.brief: Horizontal bar chart, 22 rows, sorted with worst rank (Cavalcade, 37) on top. Each bar's length = year_rank. Films labeled inline ('Cavalcade · 1933'). Highlight the 2010s entries (Spotlight, Moonlight, Argo) in a slightly stronger color. Reader can hover any bar for count and annual_share.
des_08.rationale: Lists are often boring; a sorted bar chart turns a list into a visual gradient that screams 'these are bad picks.' Highlights modern entries to make the trend land.

des_09.label: Concentration trend chart

content.interaction: hover any decade for mean / median / max share

des_09.brief: Filled area chart, decades 1920-2010 on x-axis. Y-axis: mean annual_share of the year-#1 film, formatted as percentage 0-25%. Annotate peaks: '22.6% (1970s)' and '5.7% (2010s).' Subtitle: 'the cinema-shaped hole in the culture is shrinking, too.'
des_09.rationale: Avoids the trap of saying the Academy alone is at fault — shows the broader concentration decline. Different visual mode (area) from the preceding bar charts to break up rhythm.

des_10.label: Closing image — empty filmstrip

content.prompt: A vintage black-and-white film canister on a wooden editing table. The canister is open, and faded film strip spills out across the surface, the frames empty and translucent.

des_10.brief: Quiet, restrained closing image. The empty translucent frames echo the closing argument — the canon the Academy has been writing has fewer and fewer titles people remember.
des_10.rationale: Ends the piece on mood, not data — gives the reader space after the analytical climb.

page_rhythm.tone: dark editorial cinema — deep navy + warm amber + cream, magazine-like, restrained typography
page_rhythm.text_visual_pattern: image-first hook → big stat → chart → prose-heavy methodology → analytical chart pair → image break → ranked chart → trend chart → image close
page_rhythm.anti_sameness_notes: No autoplay audio, no audio card. No video. Three images total, all atmospheric and abstract — no real film stills (copyright). Charts use restrained two-color palette (amber + cool grey/navy) so the page reads as one piece, not a chart-zoo. Uses a dumbbell chart (ana_16) and a combined two-axis chart (ana_04 + ana_12) to vary visual grammar.
page_rhythm.typography_notes: Headline serif (Playfair Display or similar). Stat callouts at 80px in amber. Inline film titles in italic. Section dividers as thin amber rules. Chart titles in small uppercase tracking.
